correctness.rationale: Reachability in an oriented tree is a partial order. Three selected vertices lie on one directed geodesic exactly when, in path order, they form a three-element reachability chain: uniqueness of the underlying tree path removes any shortcut ambiguity. Thus general-position sets are precisely two-families. Greene–Kleitman at \(k=2\) then gives the stated chain-partition minimum. An exhaustive independent finite implementation checks all three quantities on every labeled oriented tree through six vertices.

value.rationale: The 2026 primary source explicitly identifies an arbitrary oriented-tree formula as an open problem. The claim answers that tree part with a class-wide structural min–max identity, converting a directed metric problem into a classical poset two-family problem.
